19K views · 8.9K reactions | Filipino food A to Z ~ O is for Okoy/Ukoy 🦐

A Filipino deep-fried fritter that is served with a vinegar dipping sauce. It is believed that it originated in the province of Laguna and comes from the Hokkien word “ō+kuè” that means “cake made from taro”.

I personally like mine light & crunchy, therefore the batter is made with a cornstarch slurry. The trick to getting them crispy is to salt the veggies and remove as much water content as possible. I got this method from @Erwan @featrmedia recipe. I also prefer mine with unshelled shrimp but it’s traditionally made with smaller shrimp with the shell on. I am no pro chef, and not the best/fastest at cutting veggies so I used a mandoline!

Makes 7
Ingredients: 
15 shrimp, ½ chopped into bite size pieces, ½ whole
20 oz. various veggies (I used carrots, sweet potato and kalabasa squash), julienned
5 oz. bean sprouts
1 medium red onion, or 2 shallots, thinly sliced
1 bunch green onions
3 Tbsp salt
1 Tbsp fish sauce
2 tsp black or white pepper
1-2 tsp annatto powder
3/4c cold water
1.5c cornstarch
Oil for frying, I used grapeseed
Cilantro, for garnish (optional)

Full recipe is on my website at www.krizkitch.com 🥰

text: O is for okoy. Welcome back to Filipino food A to Z. Okoy or okoy is a Filipino deep-fried fritter usually made by mixing batter and shelled small shrimp in various vegetables that are deep-fried. It's believed that okoy originated in the province of Laguna and comes from the Hokkien word that means cake made from taro. I prefer a more light and crunchy okoy and therefore the batter in this recipe is made with a cornstarch slurry. The trick to getting them nice and crispy is to salt the veggies to remove as much water content and then fry them twice for that extra crunch.
